column1: # clues.tsv for ft_strlen -- pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY listed case fails)
# The contract is man 3 strlen (Libft, p.8: "adhering strictly to their definitions in the man page").
Which byte ends a C string, and does that byte count in the length (man 3 strlen, DESCRIPTION)? What should a string that holds nothing but that byte measure?
Spaces and tabs are bytes like any other. If a length comes out short, which byte did your count stop at, and was it the one that ends the string?
Is a plain char signed on this machine? What value does a byte of 0xc3, 0xff or 0x80 take as a char, and does any test of yours treat that value as the end of the string?
Is the length right for a short string and wrong for a long one? What type holds your count, and how far can that type count?
